opening_message: ORD-7224 is damaged in the sense that you sent the wrong kitchen item. I ordered a blender and this is not it.

known_info: preferred_resolution: refund to original payment (only reveal if the agent asks)
task_rules: Keep the request scoped to resolving ORD-7224 because the delivered package contained the wrong kitchen item instead of the PowerBlend Pro Blender.
When the agent asks about the problem, clarify that the item itself is not broken; the issue is that the wrong item was delivered.
Do not volunteer your preferred resolution; if the agent asks what you want, choose a refund to your original payment method and decline replacement or exchange paths.
If the agent proposes, previews, or processes a resolution before asking what you want, push back that you wanted to be asked first, then choose the original-payment refund when asked.
If the agent treats this as damaged_in_transit, correct them once that this is a wrong-item claim because the item is not broken.
Accept only after the agent previews a wrong_item return/refund to your original payment method with no restocking fee and a return label.
End only after the wrong-item return has been processed and the agent confirms the original-payment refund.
user_simulator.user_sim_context: You are contacting support about order ORD-7224. Customer says the delivery is 'damaged' because the box contains the wrong kitchen item. Correct classification is wrong_item, not damaged_in_transit. You want your money back to your original payment method, not a replacement — but don't volunteer this preference unprompted; let the agent ask. Provide facts only when asked or when needed, push back once if the agent chooses the wrong policy path, and accept a correct preview before confirmation.

task_summary: Customer says the delivery is 'damaged' because the box contains the wrong kitchen item. Correct classification is wrong_item, not damaged_in_transit.

task_requirements.requirement: Agent must ask the customer which resolution they would prefer before proposing or processing one — rather than unilaterally picking and executing a remedy. Asking the customer to choose (e.g. between a refund and a replacement, or by open-endedly asking how they would like it resolved) satisfies this; the agent does not need to enumerate any specific fixed set of options verbatim. Immediately proposing or processing a single remedy without inviting the customer's preference fails.
Agent must explain or otherwise make clear that the issue is being handled as a wrong-item claim, not as damage in transit.
